title: Legal Provisions and Safeguards in Using TraceTogether Data
what_it_is: Legal Provisions and Safeguards in Using TraceTogether Data

sections.label: TT data safeguards and penalties
sections.summary: The Government is custodian of TT data, with measures like authorised access and secured storage, and penalties for misuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Government is the custodian of the TT data submitted by individuals, and stringent measures are in place to safeguard this personal data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Examples of these measures include only allowing authorised officers to access the data, using such data only for authorised purposes and storing the data on a secured data platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Under the Public Sector (Governance) Act, public officers who recklessly or knowingly disclose the data without authorisation or misuse the data may be liable to a fine of up to $5,000 or imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

sections.label: Data taken from individuals
sections.summary: Data is taken only from the individual, extracted from witnesses but not from suspects or those under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Data will only be taken from the individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In a criminal case where there is a suspect and a witness, we will extract the data from the witness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: However, for individuals who are suspects or are under investigation, the data will not be extracted from them, for the purpose of security.

sections.label: TraceTogether use for investigations
sections.summary: TraceTogether is for contact tracing and fighting COVID-19, but police may invoke the Criminal Procedural Code for investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: TraceTogether is conceived and implemented for the purpose of contact tracing and for fighting the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We do not preclude the use of TraceTogether data in circumstances where citizens' safety and security are or have been affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Authorised police officers may invoke the Criminal Procedural Code, as I had mentioned earlier, to obtain this data for the purpose of criminal investigation and for the purpose of protecting the safety and security of our citizens.
